name: scenario_generator_output
description: Return the generated edge-case scenarios. Use this tool for every response: it is the only way to deliver scenarios.

Expectation.description: What a correct system would do — never what the buggy target does.

expected_status.description: HTTP status codes a correct implementation may return for the action.
expected_status.title: Expected Status

expected_behavior.description: One or two sentences on correct behaviour, in terms a reviewer can check against the recorded response. Used by the LLM judge.
expected_behavior.title: Expected Behavior

invariants.description: Checkable statements about state after the action, e.g. 'sum of both balances is unchanged'. Verified against `probes` output.
invariants.title: Invariants

probes.description: Read-only calls run after the action to observe resulting state.
probes.title: Probes

Expectation.title: Expectation

HttpStep.description:
One HTTP call.

`path` and string values inside `body` / `query` may contain `{name}`
placeholders, resolved by Execution from earlier steps' `save` captures.

name.description: Short snake_case label, unique within the scenario.
name.title: Name

save.description: Capture values from this step's JSON response for later steps: {"src_id": "id"} reads the response field `id` and binds it to {src_id}. Dotted paths index nested objects, e.g. 'data.account.id'.
save.title: Save

HttpStep.title: HttpStep

ScenarioCategory.description: The 7 QE categories every ScenarioSet must cover (Master Plan v7).
ScenarioCategory.title: ScenarioCategory

ScenarioDraft.description:
The per-scenario wire format: `repeat` and `concurrency` are required.

On `Scenario` both fields default to 1, which is right for a scenario
written by hand or read back from a file. But a defaulted field is an
optional field, and the generator left both out of all 14 scenarios —
including one titled "Many parallel transfers racing" — even after the
prompt spelled the requirement out in two places. A set where every
scenario is concurrency=1, repeat=1 cannot reach a race or a double-spend
however its categories are labelled.

Dropping the defaults makes the model state a number per scenario, so the
decision is taken rather than skipped. Whether the set as a whole actually
exercises a race and a replay is a policy question, checked by the
generator's validator where a correction can be fed back and retried.

id.description: Stable id, lowercase slug, e.g. 'sc-001' or 'sc-overdraft'.
id.title: Id

title.description: One short line naming what is probed.
title.title: Title

rationale.description: Why this is worth testing — the failure mode it would expose.
rationale.title: Rationale

repeat.description: Send the action N times (idempotency / replay). 1 = once.
repeat.title: Repeat

concurrency.description: Send the action N times in parallel (race). 1 = no race.
concurrency.title: Concurrency

input_schema.description:
The generator's wire format — just the scenarios.

This is what the model fills in via the forced tool call; run metadata
(target, model, timestamp) is attached by code afterwards, so the model
cannot get it wrong. `extra="forbid"` turns silent field drift into a
validation error the retry can act on.
